groundingNote: The brand is a three-part baseline-aligned typographic compound (amber mono chip + display wordmark + mono sub-label), not a logo; the terminal chrome has selectively hollow traffic-light dots (only the third filled amber); step-heads use a CSS ::before zero-pad so numbers are rendered as 01/02/03 in amber mono at 14px — a restrained fixed-width prefix, not a large decorative numeral; and amber is enforced as a singleton accent via a named CSS custom property with an explicit comment 'THE single signal accent'.

brand: Sticky header band where brand is PURELY typographic: a monospace chip/badge (short code, border-outlined, no icon) + condensed uppercase display wordmark + small monospace sub-label — all baseline-aligned in one horizontal group; reject patterns where an icon or glyph leads
Mixed font-family lockup: mono for the badge/chip, a condensed or wide-display family for the primary name, mono for the sub-label — the typographic contrast IS the brand identity
Amber (or equivalent single warm accent) used only on the chip/badge and the accent syllable of the wordmark — not as a background fill on the whole header
Background treatment: panel-tone header separated from page ground by a single hairline rule, possibly a very faint vertical gradient toward transparent — not a thick colored bar or drop shadow
step-heads: Number is a small (12–15px) fixed-width prefix in monospace accent color, zero-padded (01/02/03), baseline-aligned with the h2 — NOT a large decorative numeral floated left or centered above
h2 in a condensed or wide-display family, uppercase, weight 600–700, ~22–28px, immediately adjacent to the number with a tight gap (~12–16px)
One-line description in a body-weight sans at ~13–14px in a subdued secondary tone, sitting 6–10px below the h2 — not a full paragraph, not bold

The entire step-head is flush-left with no enclosing card or box; the body panel (step-body) is a separate bordered block below it; hierarchy is achieved through typography alone, not spatial containers around the head
terminal-preview: Chrome bar with three distinct regions: traffic-light dots (left) / centered monospace uppercase title / inline control (right, e.g. a range slider with a cols-badge) — all in a single bar, NOT split across two rows

Traffic-light dots that are partially hollow — at least one or two rendered as border-only circles with transparent fill; the active/filled dot in an accent color rather than the conventional green; this signals 'restrained, non-literal' chrome
Preview body set on a darker background than the chrome bar and surrounding panel (ground-dark under the chrome's panel-hi), creating a recessed well effect with the content appearing inset
Range slider for viewport/column width control sitting inline in the chrome bar itself (not below the preview), with accent-colored thumb/track and a small monospace badge showing the live value
Bottom footnote in monospace at ~11px in a subdued tone, separated by a hairline — 'Approximate' or equivalent disclaimer; confirms this is a live-render element, not a static mockup

acceptNuance: Accept a fine engineering-grid substrate (40–50px repeating line grid in a near-invisible tone) as intentional texture — it reads as instrument-grade, not decorative noise; pieces with this pattern score above flat-dark equivalents
Accept amber-singleton design systems where amber is provably the only accent across the entire UI — multi-accent dark UIs (teal + amber + purple status dots) score lower even if otherwise restrained

Accept typographic brand lockups that mix two or three font families in a single horizontal compound — this is the structural pattern here, and hunting only single-family brands will miss the right reference class

Accept toggle switches and interactive controls where STATE is carried by position/shape first, color second — the knob-position-primary pattern is an accessibility and instrument-grade signal worth filtering for

Prefer pieces where the terminal/preview chrome is minimal-literal: three dots are present but not colorful traffic-lights; the chrome is identifiable as terminal but does not cosplay macOS — restrained signification over fidelity

Accept zero-padded sequence markers (01 02 03) as functional step indicators when they are small and typographically subordinate to the step title — reject pieces where large numerals are the hero visual of the section
